title: CLAUDE.md
text: 1. Fisher-Scoring Iteration: Fay-Herriot estimation uses Fisher-scoring algorithm implemented C++ speed. algorithm iterates estimate random effect variance (sigma²), computes EBLUPs. 2. Spatial Weight Matrix: Spatial models require row-standardized proximity matrix W. spatial models, matrix must cover domains (including unsampled), just sampled ones—code handles unsampled areas borrowing strength spatial neighbors. 3. Bootstrap Parallelization: Parametric non-parametric bootstrap MSE use OpenMP via RcppParallel. n_threads parameter controls parallelism; n_threads = 0 uses available cores. 4. Unsampled Domain Handling: - Fay-Herriot (eblup_fh): Uses synthetic estimators areas NA response - Spatial FH (eblup_sfh): Uses spatial kriging (full-spatial synthetic) unsampled areas - Spatio-Temporal FH (eblup_stfh): support unsampled domains (complete panel required) 5. Output Structure: fitting functions return list class fastsae containing: - df_eblup: Data frame estimates (eblup, mse, rse) - estcoef: Regression coefficients SE, z-value, p-value - random_effect_var: Estimated variance random effects - goodness: Log-likelihood, AIC, BIC - n_iter, convergence: Convergence information

what: Architectural Insights: Why is fastsae so Fast?
title: Performance & Scalability Benchmarks
text: Compiled C++ Linear Solvers: Instead interpreting nested loops R, fastsae implements Fisher-scoring parameter search Woodbury identity matrix inversions Armadillo C++, directly leveraging optimized BLAS/LAPACK routines. Zero-Copy Matrix Operations: Memory allocations large intermediate structures (VV, V−1V^{-1}, PP) avoided reused across Fisher iterations rather reallocated heap. OpenMP Multi-Threaded Bootstrap: Bootstrap resampling runs natively parallel across CPU cores using #pragma omp parallel , avoiding serialization overhead R worker processes (parallel::makeCluster / foreach). Woodbury Identity Panel Data: eblup_stfh, inversion block (DT×DT)(DT \times DT) covariance matrix VV reduced operations individual D×DD \times D T×TT \times T blocks via Kronecker Woodbury decomposition, transforming O((DT)3)O((DT)^3) bottleneck scalable O(D3+T3)O(D^3 + T^3) steps. Integrated Nested Laplace Approximations (INLA): complex hierarchical generalized spatio-temporal models (ebp_area), fastsae utilizes INLA compute analytical posterior margins directly sparse Gaussian Markov Random Fields, bypassing Monte Carlo sampling entirely.

title: Bayesian Area-Level Small Area Estimation with INLA
text: Classical Small Area Estimation (SAE) models—Fay-Herriot (1979) model—traditionally assume Gaussian distribution direct survey estimators known sampling error variances. However, real-world official statistics frequently encounter non-Gaussian indicators: - Poverty rates, unemployment rates, prevalence ratios: strictly bounded open interval (0,1)(0, 1). - Disease counts, crime incidents, rare events: discrete counts subject Poisson Negative Binomial overdispersion population exposures. - Binary survey aggregates: proportions derived small sample sizes (Binomial trials). - Skewed economic expenditures: strictly positive continuous outcomes (Gamma). Furthermore, data collected across geographical areas repeated time (panel/longitudinal surveys), outcomes exhibit spatial dependency temporal autocorrelation. fastsae package introduces ebp_area(), unified hierarchical Bayesian framework powered Integrated Nested Laplace Approximations (INLA). provides fast, deterministic, highly accurate analytical posterior approximations without computational bottlenecks, convergence diagnostics, chain-tuning associated Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC).

title: Model Diagnostics and Residual Analysis
text: Small Area Estimation (SAE), model-based estimators borrow strength across domains time improve estimation precision direct survey estimators. However, introducing model assumptions carries risk model misspecification, bias, inappropriate shrinkage. address challenges, fastsae provides unified diagnostic framework centered diagnose() function dedicated S3 autoplot() visualization method. evaluates frequentist C++ EBLUP models (eblup_fh, eblup_sfh, eblup_stfh, eblup_bhf) Bayesian INLA EBP models (ebp_area).

title: Model Diagnostics and Residual Analysis
text: diagnostic workflow evaluates four fundamental dimensions SAE model quality: Precision Gain & RSE Reduction: Quantifies improvement Relative Standard Error (RSE=MSEθ̂×100%\text{RSE} = \frac{\sqrt{\text{MSE}}}{\hat{\theta}} \times 100\%) compared direct survey estimates. Evaluates whether areas satisfy official statistics reliability threshold (typically RSE<25%\text{RSE} < 25\% 20%20\%). External Calibration & Bias Diagnostic (Brown et al., 2001): Tests whether model predictions statistically unbiased predictors direct estimates using regression: yd=α+βθ̂d+edy_d = \alpha + \beta \hat{\theta}_d + e_d unbiasedness, joint hypothesis H0:α=0,β=1H_0: \alpha = 0, \beta = 1 rejected. Goodness--Fit Statistic: Computes Chi-square diagnostic statistic WW: W=∑d=1D(yd−θ̂d)2Vd+MSE(θ̂d)W = \sum_{d=1}^D \frac{(y_d - \hat{\theta}_d)^2}{V_d + \text{MSE}(\hat{\theta}_d)} approximately follows χ2(D)\chi^2(D) distribution null hypothesis proper model specification. Residual Spatial Autocorrelation (Moran’s ): Verifies whether spatial autocorrelation fully captured model random effects. Significant residual spatial clustering indicates unmodeled spatial patterns remain.

title: Spatial and Spatio-Temporal Models
text: Spatial Fay-Herriot model (Pratesi & Salvati, 2008) models area random effects using Simultaneous Autoregressive (SAR(1)) process: y=Xβ+u+ey = X\beta + u + e u=ρ1Wu+ϵ1⟹u=(−ρ1W)−1ϵ1u = \rho_1 W u + \epsilon_1 \implies u = (- \rho_1 W)^{-1} \epsilon_1 : - WW known row-standardized spatial proximity matrix (D×DD \times D). - ρ1∈(−1,1)\rho_1 \(-1, 1) spatial autoregressive parameter. - ϵ1∼N(0,σu12ID)\epsilon_1 \sim N(0, \sigma_{u1}^2 I_D) independent innovation noise. - e∼N(0,Ve)e \sim N(0, V_e) sampling error diagonal matrix Ve=diag(D1,…,DD)V_e = \text{diag}(D_1, \dots, D_D).

N(0,Ddt)e_{dt} \sim \text{ind. } N(0, D_{dt}) sampling errors.

text: Unlike area-level models aggregate data prior modeling, unit-level models operate directly individual survey unit records (e.g., households, farms, persons) linking population auxiliary aggregates (e.g., census means satellite imagery). fastsae package implements nested error regression model Battese, Harter, Fuller (1988) via eblup_bhf(), providing fast estimation parallel parametric bootstrap MSE.

N(0,σu2)u_d \sim \text{..d. } N(0, \sigma_u^2) area-specific random effect. - edj∼..d. N(0,σe2)e_{dj} \sim \text{..d. } N(0, \sigma_e^2) unit-level error variance. - udu_d edje_{dj} mutually independent. small area population mean Y‾d\bar{Y}_d estimated : Y‾̂dEBLUP=X‾d⊤β̂+γd(y‾d−x‾d⊤β̂)\hat{\bar{Y}}_d^{\text{EBLUP}} = \bar{X}_d^\top \hat{\beta} + \gamma_d (\bar{y}_d - \bar{x}_d^\top \hat{\beta}) : - X‾d\bar{X}_d known population mean vector auxiliary variables domain dd. - y‾d\bar{y}_d x‾d\bar{x}_d sample means domain dd. - γd=σu2σu2+σe2/nd\gamma_d = \frac{\sigma_u^2}{\sigma_u^2 + \sigma_e^2 / n_d} shrinkage ratio.

text: formula object class formula specifying fixed-effects model (e.g., y ~ x1 + x2). data data.frame containing area-level data (one row per area). domain Vector, column name, one-sided formula referencing area/domain identifier data. NULL, domains numbered consecutively. time Vector, column name, one-sided formula referencing time period identifier data (e.g. time = "year" ~year). Required temporal != "none". family Character string specifying response distribution / likelihood. Options: "gaussian": Continuous response (Fay-Herriot model). vardir     provided, sampling variances treated known. vardir = NULL,     residual variance estimated. "binomial": Binary / proportion response. Requires trials. "poisson": Count response / disease rate. Supports exposure. "nbinomial": Negative Binomial overdispersed counts. "beta": Continuous proportions strictly (0, 1). vardir     provided, area-specific precision calculated via Janicki (2020) formula     \(\phi_i = y_i(1 - y_i)/V_i - 1\) injected via INLA's scale argument.     trials provided, precision scaled \(n_i - 1\). "gamma": Skewed positive continuous response. spatial Character string specifying spatial random effect structure: "none": Non-spatial IID area random intercept (default). "bym2": Scaled Besag-York-Mollié 2 model (Riebler et al., 2016),     decomposing area variance spatial (\(\phi\)) unstructured components. "bym": Classic Besag-York-Mollié (1991) model. "besag": Intrinsic Conditional Autoregressive (ICAR) model. "generic1": Leroux spatial autoregressive model. temporal Character string specifying temporal random effect structure: "none": temporal random effect (default cross-sectional model). "rw1": First-order random walk across time periods. "rw2": Second-order random walk across time periods. "ar1": First-order autoregressive process across time periods. "iid": Unstructured independent time effects. st_interaction Character string specifying spatio-temporal structure: "none": Additive main spatial temporal effects (default). "domain-specific": Domain-specific temporal random walk / AR(1) dynamics     shared variance parameter (directly corresponds tipsae spatio-temporal model). "separable": Grouped dynamic spatial field evolving time via AR(1) / RW     (corresponds classical Spatio-Temporal Fay-Herriot models, Marhuenda et al. 2013). "type1": Knorr-Held (2000) Type interaction (unstructured space \(\times\) unstructured time). "type2": Knorr-Held Type II interaction (unstructured space \(\times\) structured time). "type3": Knorr-Held Type III interaction (structured space \(\times\) unstructured time). "type4": Knorr-Held Type IV interaction (structured space \(\times\) structured time). W Proximity spatial adjacency matrix. Can square matrix, Matrix, spdep nb listw object. Dimensions must match total number domains data. Required spatial != "none". vardir Vector, column name, formula specifying sampling variances direct estimator (family = "gaussian" family = "beta"). trials Vector, column name, formula specifying sample sizes / total trials per area (family = "binomial"). exposure Vector, column name, formula specifying expected counts population exposure offsets (family = "poisson" "nbinomial"). method Estimation method: "inla" (Bayesian INLA, default) "laplace" (Frequentist GLMM Laplace approximation via lme4). strategy INLA approximation strategy: "simplified.laplace" (fast default), "laplace" (full Laplace approximation), "gaussian". link Optional character string link function. NULL, default canonical link used (identity Gaussian, logit Binomial/Beta, log Poisson/NegBinom/Gamma). scale_model Logical. TRUE (default), scales spatial graph marginal variance structured effect approximately 1 (recommended BYM2/Besag). prior_prec List specifying prior random effect precision. Default Penalized Complexity (PC) prior: list(prior = "pc.prec", param = c(1, 0.01)). prior_phi List specifying PC-prior spatial mixing parameter \(\phi\) BYM2 model. Default list(prior = "pc", param = c(0.5, 0.5)). prior_rho Optional list specifying prior spatial autocorrelation parameter (generic1/slm). prior_prec_time Optional list specifying prior temporal precision. Default PC prior: list(prior = "pc.prec", param = c(1, 0.01)). prior_rho_time Optional list specifying prior temporal autocorrelation parameter AR(1). print_result Logical. TRUE (default), prints summary results. ... Additional arguments passed INLA::inla().

title: Simulate Spatial Proximity and Adjacency Matrices — sim_spatial_weights
text: Generates synthetic spatial proximity adjacency matrices   small area estimation models. Supports k-nearest neighbors (KNN) random   2D coordinates, regular grid contiguity (lattice), 1D circular rings.

title: Simulate Spatial Proximity and Adjacency Matrices — sim_spatial_weights
code: sim_spatial_weights(   D = 40,   type = c("knn", "grid", "ring"),   style = c("B", "W"),   k = 4,   coords = NULL,   seed = NULL )

title: Simulate Spatial Proximity and Adjacency Matrices — sim_spatial_weights
text: D Integer. Number small areas (domains). Default 40. type Character. Topology type: "knn" (k-nearest neighbors 2D coordinates), "grid" (Rook contiguity regular 2D lattice), "ring" (1D circular chain). Default "knn". style Character. Weight style: "B" symmetric binary adjacency (0/1) zero diagonal (standard INLA graph models BYM2, BYM, Besag), "W" row-standardized weights (sum row equals 1, standard SAR/SLM models). Default "B". k Integer. Number nearest neighbors per domain type = "knn". Default 4. Must 1 D - 1. coords Optional numeric matrix dimension c(D, 2) containing 2D spatial coordinates. provided type = "knn", distances computed coordinates. seed Optional integer. Random seed reproducible coordinate generation.

title: Simulate Spatial Proximity and Adjacency Matrices — sim_spatial_weights
text: square numeric matrix dimension \(D \times D\) row column names   set domain identifiers ("1", "2", ..., "D").   Attributes include "coords" (2D coordinates) "type".

title: Simulate Spatial Proximity and Adjacency Matrices — sim_spatial_weights
text: type = "knn", coordinates sampled \(\text{Uniform}(0, 1)^2\) provided. domain connected \(k\) nearest neighbors. ensure symmetric adjacency graph required GMRF spatial priors (INLA), edges made mutual: domain \(\) \(j\) connected \(j\) among \(k\) nearest neighbors \(\) vice versa. type = "grid", domains placed regular \(r \times c\) lattice \(r = \lfloor\sqrt{D}\rfloor\) \(c = \lceil D / r \rceil\). \(r \times c > D\), first \(D\) lattice points retained. Rook contiguity (sharing common edge) used. type = "ring", domain \(\) connected \(-1\) \(+1\) closed ring.
